meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я бы хотел помочь вам.
examples.trans: I would like to help you.

examples.text: Просто хотел поближе познакомиться.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to get better acquainted.

examples.text: Если ты сам не хочешь, тебе никто не сможет помочь.
examples.trans: If you don't want it yourself, nobody will be able to help you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nobody') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Да пока ты на складе, никто ничего не поймёт.
examples.trans: As long as you are in the storage room, nobody will figure anything out.

examples.text: Если ты сам не хочешь, тебе никто не сможет помочь.
examples.trans: If you don't want it yourself, nobody will be able to help you.

examples.text: Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be able', forming an aspectual pair with 'мочь'.

examples.text: Если ты сам не хочешь, тебе никто не сможет помочь.
examples.trans: If you don't want it yourself, nobody will be able to help you.

examples.text: Мы приехали сразу, как смогли.
examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.

examples.text: Ты сможешь прийти завтра утром?
examples.trans: Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Я бы хотел помочь вам.
examples.trans: I would like to help you.

examples.text: А то ведь уволят. И Елена Павловна не поможет.
examples.trans: Otherwise they will fire you. And Elena Pavlovna won't be able to help.

examples.text: Слышь ты! Хотя ты прав, не поможет.
examples.trans: Listen here! Though you are right, she won't help.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'free', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ты свободен. На все четыре стороны.
examples.trans: You are free. Free to go wherever you please.

examples.text: Всё, свободен!
examples.trans: That's all, you can go!

examples.text: Это место свободно?
examples.trans: Is this seat free?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я согласен на всё.
examples.trans: I agree to everything.

examples.text: Мне кажется, все уже догадались.
examples.trans: I think everyone has already guessed.

examples.text: Нагиев весь персонал собирает.
examples.trans: Nagiyev is gathering the entire staff.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'four', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты свободен. На все четыре стороны.
examples.trans: You are free. Free to go wherever you please.

examples.text: Четыре года.
examples.trans: Four years.

examples.text: У меня четыре фломастера.
examples.trans: I have four markers.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'side', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты свободен. На все четыре стороны.
examples.trans: You are free. Free to go wherever you please.

examples.text: С другой стороны, это интересно.
examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.

examples.text: Магазин на той стороне.
examples.trans: The shop is on that side.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'thank you', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо. До свидания.
examples.trans: Thank you. Goodbye.

examples.text: Спасибо, папа!
examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!

examples.text: Спасибо за доверие!
examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: До дома подбросите?
examples.trans: Will you give me a ride home?

examples.text: Спасибо. До свидания.
examples.trans: Thank you. Goodbye.

examples.text: До свидания!
examples.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'meeting' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо. До свидания.
examples.trans: Thank you. Goodbye.

examples.text: До свидания!
examples.trans: Goodbye!

examples.text: У меня сегодня свидание.
examples.trans: I have a date today.
